title: Efficient Memory Integration: MRAM-SRAM Hybrid Accelerator for Sparse On-Device Learning
problem: NVM-based PIM accelerators suffer from high write energy, latency, and instability for on-device learning, while SRAM designs have high leakage currents and large memory footprints. A hybrid approach is needed to balance storage efficiency with computation speed for training tasks.
motivation: On-device continual learning enables edge devices to perform training locally, reducing latency and privacy concerns.
method: The design combines NVM and SRAM in a hybrid PIM architecture with fully-digital sparse processing supporting N:M structured sparsity patterns. Circuit macros enable both storage and computation using sparsity, leveraging NVM's low leakage for storage and SRAM's speed for training operations.
key_novelty: First fully-digital sparse processing in memory design using hybrid NVM-SRAM architecture for on-device continual learning.
contributions: Hybrid NVM-SRAM PIM accelerator architecture combining benefits of both memory types
Circuit macros supporting N:M structured sparsity in both storage and computation
Reduced area and power consumption for on-device learning applications
Scalable solution maintaining high accuracy across training tasks
primary_theme: hybrid-memory PIM for efficient on-device learning
